aspects.says: When parsing, dd demands two digits, while d also accepts a single digit.
basis: section:ofPattern Turns 30 February Into the 28th Unless the Resolver Is STRICT, and STRICT Needs uuuu

aspects.says: A DateTimeFormatter is immutable, so one static final instance is safe on every thread, and withLocale or withZone return a new formatter whose result must be kept.
basis: section:Month and Day Names Come From a Locale, So Name One

aspects.says: A pattern formatter prints an Instant only after withZone gives it a zone.
basis: section:An Offset in the Text Is Part of the Value, So Parse Into a Type That Keeps It

aspects.says: The ISO_* constants cover the standard machine formats and resolve STRICT.
aspects.reason: a lookup table of constants with nothing to decide; the timestamp practice already reads ISO offset text

aspects.says: Pattern letters are case-sensitive: MM is the month and mm the minute, HH the 24-hour hour and hh the 12-hour one that needs a.
basis: section:Pattern Letters Are Case-Sensitive, and YYYY Is the Year of the Week

aspects.says: Month and day names come from the formatter's locale, the JVM default when none is given; English locales disagree (Sep and Sept), Locale.ROOT has no full names, and parsing names is case-sensitive unless the formatter is built case-insensitive.
basis: section:Month and Day Names Come From a Locale, So Name One

aspects.says: Text with an offset is parsed into OffsetDateTime, ZonedDateTime or Instant; LocalDateTime drops the offset silently, and a pattern with xxx refuses Z.
basis: section:An Offset in the Text Is Part of the Value, So Parse Into a Type That Keeps It

aspects.says: A formatter from ofPattern resolves SMART and turns a day the month lacks into the month's last day; ResolverStyle.STRICT refuses it.
basis: section:ofPattern Turns 30 February Into the 28th Unless the Resolver Is STRICT, and STRICT Needs uuuu

aspects.says: STRICT with yyyy and no era field refuses every date, because a year-of-era needs an era STRICT won't assume; uuuu works.
basis: section:ofPattern Turns 30 February Into the 28th Unless the Resolver Is STRICT, and STRICT Needs uuuu

aspects.says: YYYY is the week-based year, whose weeks come from the formatter's locale, so it prints the next year in the last days of December (or the previous one in the first days of January); the calendar year is uuuu or yyyy.
basis: section:Pattern Letters Are Case-Sensitive, and YYYY Is the Year of the Week
